target_customer: Municipal governments and traffic departments that operate signalized intersections
problem: Most traffic signals run on fixed timing plans and old loop detectors, which causes delays and unsafe crossings and generates resident complaints. Studies and retiming are manual and expensive for cities.
business_model: B2B and government software and hardware subscription per intersection (pricing not public)
product_category: AI traffic signal control using cameras and computer vision

founders.name: Collin Barnwell
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built safety-critical IoT and camera devices and interned at Handshake and G2 when each had fewer than five engineers. Education not listed.

founders.name: Sabeek Pradhan
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built vehicle, pedestrian and bike detection and tracking for driverless vehicles. Education not listed.

competitors.name: Miovision Surtrac
competitors.what: Decentralized AI adaptive signal control from the Carnegie Mellon spinout Rapid Flow, sold by Miovision
competitors.traction_then: Deployed in many US cities, from the Pittsburgh origin onward
competitors.funding_then: Miovision is a funded private company; amount not checked

competitors.name: NoTraffic
competitors.what: All in one hardware and software AI traffic management platform
competitors.funding_then: Series A of 17.5M USD in July 2021 per TechCrunch

competitors.name: Rhythm Engineering InSync
competitors.what: Adaptive signal control sold to counties
competitors.traction_then: Listed among recommended providers in a Broward County study

technical_complexity.rationale: Safety-critical real time perception and control at intersections using cameras, a 3D model and simulation, with municipal deployment constraints.

defensibility.rationale: Established vendors already sell adaptive control. A camera-only approach with no special hardware is a differentiator but not yet a structural moat; city pilots and references are the main asset.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were already selling adaptive systems in 2024. Roundabout had no reported takeover as of the sources reviewed.

market_need_then: Cities face pedestrian deaths and resident complaints about specific intersections; the San Anselmo pilot at The Hub, running since August 2025 per local news, was driven by complaints. Adaptive systems cost an estimated 30,000 to 60,000 USD per intersection per one analyst, which leaves room for cheaper entrants.

identity.logo: A plain letter R mark appears on one directory; official logo not confirmed

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; the name is a traffic term that fits the product but is generic and shared with other companies.

outcome_analysis: Roundabout is an early stage YC Fall 2024 company with an active first deployment in San Anselmo, California, and founders with autonomy and perception experience from Waymo, Zoox and Google. No exit, shutdown or later round was found. Outcome is open: selling to cities is slow, but the claim of no special hardware could lower cost against incumbents.
notes: Funding: VCBacked and StandOut list 500K USD pre-seed in December 2024 with YC and Unpopular Ventures, and Seedtable lists a different figure; only aggregators, so unverified and not recorded as a round.
